scope: Independent mathematical audit and conditional extension. No state-machine acceptance or proof of RH.

claims.statement: Strong Nyman–Beurling criterion with integer dilations
claims.assumptions: L²(0,∞), closure of the linear span of integer dilates, χ=1_(0,1].
claims.downstream_action: Cite the theorem with the ambient space and closure.

claims.statement: Zero-tail coordinate, coefficient rigidity, L6 obstruction
claims.proof_or_counterexample: Subtract the norm-controlled slope times {x}; integer differences are 1/k−1_{k|d}. Möbius inversion yields −δnk, and the L6 dual squared norm is 92.
claims.downstream_action: Any successful sequence has coefficient limit −μ(n); deleting 6 costs at least 1/92.

claims.statement: Prime-only uniform separation and three full integer candidates
claims.assumptions: Finite prime columns plus exact constraint for all primes beyond the test window. Infinite tail included in upper bounds.
claims.proof_or_counterexample: Frozen rational certificates rerun. Their rational upper bounds are strictly below the prime-only lower bound.
claims.downstream_action: Keep three candidate upper bounds distinct from optima.

claims.statement: Finite-horizon rank-one future port and calibration capacity
claims.assumptions: Finite positive M for the port. PNT for the limiting capacity.
claims.proof_or_counterexample: On prefix r_n(m)=m/n for n>M. Difference functionals recover all earlier columns. Summation by parts identifies the sharp squared norm; mesh jumps μ(k) give 15/π² (return §3).
claims.downstream_action: Do not collapse the same coordinates on enlarged horizons.

claims.statement: Square integrability of the positive arithmetic road and converse
claims.assumptions: a>0; unconditional L² for a≥1/2; also 0<a<1/2 under RH; a sequence tending to zero suffices for the converse.
claims.proof_or_counterexample: Finite floors plus an absolutely convergent tail identify f_a(1/x)=cx−S_a(x). Burnol math/0202166 §4, lemmas 4.1–4.3, theorems 4.1 and 4.2.
claims.downstream_action: Use the critical-line Mellin identity only after L² membership has been established.

claims.statement: The Chebyshev boundary derivative has infinite road energy
claims.assumptions: Pointwise derivative, x>0 fixed; saddle at infinity must be considered separately.
claims.proof_or_counterexample: Brent–Platt–Trudgian arXiv:2008.06140, Thm 1 and §4 (also off RH), dyadic shell lower bound X²/5374.
claims.downstream_action: Do not interchange the derivative with the global road norm.

claims.statement: Completed Schur, Pick and zero-Gram kernels
claims.assumptions: Forward direction assumes RH. Converse assumes holomorphic contractive quotients at a sequence a↓0 throughout the right half-plane.
claims.proof_or_counterexample: Modulus of paired xi product factors grows horizontally. Shifted off-line zeros would force accumulated numerator zeros. Logarithmic derivative of paired factors gives Gram sum.
claims.downstream_action: Use completed ratios. No positive raw Weil matrix follows.

claims.statement: Positive road contact hierarchy and absolute penetration boundary
claims.assumptions: 0<a<1 for the absolute tail bound; n>1 for first positive contact; Re s>1 for Dirichlet coefficient differentiation.
claims.proof_or_counterexample: Multiply local factors. Absolute divisor truncation gives |S_a−cx| ≪_a x^(1−a); shifted nontrivial zero β−a<1−a.
claims.downstream_action: Use asymptotic cancellation to go farther; absolute control only covers stated half-plane.

claims.statement: Local zero cluster has the multiplicity profile (iu/(1+iu))^m
claims.assumptions: For the road-norm interpretation assume RH; zero ordinates are distinct and signed.
claims.proof_or_counterexample: Factor ζ as a power times a local nonzero analytic function and rescale the horizontal shift.

claims.statement: Completed defect slope passes through the full sum and yields raw slope
claims.assumptions: RH; 0<a≤1/2 for the summable majorant; count multiplicities once for each distinct ordinate.
claims.proof_or_counterexample: Disjoint intervals give the finite lower bound; Cauchy convolution and the paired log derivative dominate the tail; Poisson identity and completion error finish.
claims.downstream_action: First-order slope equals λ1 exactly under simplicity within RH.

claims.statement: Effective range of A(a), and the removable zero of J in log differentiation
claims.assumptions: Positive real a. Near a=1/2,t=0 differentiate J itself.
claims.proof_or_counterexample: Uniform gamma ratio asymptotics give A finite exactly for a<1, (1−a)A²→1/(2π²), and A/a→a strictly positive derivative norm at zero.
claims.downstream_action: Keep the explicit U_road threshold finite only on 0<a<1.

claims.statement: Finite Green energy and minimum over constant backgrounds
claims.assumptions: M≥2, continuous background on (0,M), endpoint atoms have zero kernel weight.
claims.proof_or_counterexample: Integrate the product of two cumulative indicators; background integral is log(M/n), constant-density double integral is M.
claims.downstream_action: Use monotone unminimized energies for completeness, minimized ones only for sufficient falsification.

claims.assumptions: RH in the Schur estimate, 0<a<1 for the finite threshold. Converse square integrability from countable inequalities has no RH hypothesis.
claims.proof_or_counterexample: Triangular norm inequality and |C|≤1 give an O(a) norm error. Reverse via Burnol 4.2.
claims.downstream_action: Use U_road for arithmetic Q; upper bound for the completed energy alone is insufficient.

claims.statement: Exact weighted midpoint correction and its sign
claims.assumptions: a>0, either energy finite for difference of the infinite series; finite truncation holds for every a.
claims.proof_or_counterexample: Q−D=c²(1+ζ(2)/12)−Σ∫E²w; the first cell alone costs 4c²/3. Finite integral stops at M+1.
claims.downstream_action: Preserve the (0,1) term. At finite energy D exceeds Q by at least (1/3−ζ(2)/12)c².

claims.statement: Signed two-term difference Q−D=C_cell a²+O(a³); D shares the raw multiplicity slope
claims.proof_or_counterexample: Use X=floor(a⁻²); BPT dyadic RH mean square controls the Taylor cross term. The unexpanded tail after extra inverse-power weighting is O(a). Return §1.
claims.downstream_action: Use C_cell for discretization, without interpreting it as the second coefficient of Q or D individually.

claims.statement: Direct O(a) bound for the escaping unweighted infinite-horizon energy
claims.assumptions: No assumption of RH or an equivalent estimate.
claims.proof_or_counterexample: Fixed horizons are O_M(a²). The controlled difference has an extra inverse power, unavailable in the full sum.
claims.downstream_action: Requires uniform cancellation across growing horizons.

claims.statement: Identify the Ramanujan expansion with the actual arithmetic sequence in B²
claims.assumptions: a>0. For each fixed n the Euler product converges absolutely.
claims.proof_or_counterexample: Finite-prime products approximate R_a in B² with squared error ≤Σ_{p>Y}p^(−1−a); use CRT then B² continuity. Square-summability by itself gives only an abstract limit.
claims.downstream_action: Use the prime truncation before replacing the sequence by its spectral expansion.

claims.statement: Translation-averaged response and finite phase witness
claims.assumptions: a>0 for the road summation; general real periodic sequences for the counterexample.
claims.proof_or_counterexample: The fixed-H B² operator is bounded, Tonelli applies to diagonal powers. The translates (1,−1,0) and (−1,0,1) give unequal fixed-origin energies while all modal powers match.
claims.downstream_action: Retain phases on the full periodic class.

claims.statement: Nonfactorization from powers on the restricted one-parameter road itself
claims.assumptions: Only the image of a↦R_a is admissible.
claims.proof_or_counterexample: The finite periodic example is outside this restricted family. Different sufficient conditions on two energies alone do not preclude reconstruction.
claims.downstream_action: Seek a family-specific witness or a rigorous statement about an enlarged observation class.
